tc_benefit: Backend services (vets, visits, customers, genai) can be split, moved, renamed or replaced, and retry/circuit-breaker policy changed, by editing one gateway configuration instead of every client.
tc_conditions: Materialises when the backend topology changes, a service is added or replaced, or a policy such as retry, timeouts or circuit breaking must change for all routes. Assumes clients call the gateway rather than the services directly.
tc_signals: lb:// routes to vets-service, visits-service, customers-service, genai-service
default filters CircuitBreaker and Retry applied across routes

tc_benefit: The admin-server takes its settings from a central config server, so URLs, credentials and tuning values can change per environment without rebuilding or redeploying it.
tc_conditions: Materialises when the same build runs in several environments, or a setting must change quickly in production. Assumes the config server is deployed and serves properties for admin-server.

tc_benefit: The api-gateway loads its settings from a central config server, so routes, URLs and credentials can change per environment from one place without rebuilding the gateway.
tc_conditions: Pays off when the same build is deployed to several environments, or when a gateway setting must change quickly in production. Assumes the config server is actually deployed and serves a config for api-gateway.

tc_benefit: Settings such as URLs, credentials and tuning values can be changed per environment from the central config server without rebuilding or redeploying customers-service.
tc_conditions: Materialises when the same build runs in several environments (the default profile and a docker-style profile point at different config server URLs) or when a setting must change quickly in production. Assumes the config server is actually deployed and serves customers-service properties.
tc_signals: spring.config.import optional:configserver: with ${CONFIG_SERVER_URL} override in application.yml

tc_benefit: Discovery-server settings can be changed per environment from the central config server without rebuilding or redeploying the service.
tc_conditions: Materialises when the same build runs in several environments (e.g. local vs docker profiles) or a setting must change quickly in production; assumes a config server is actually running and serves config for this service.

tc_benefit: Settings such as URLs, credentials and tuning values can change per environment or at run time from the config server, without rebuilding or redeploying genai-service.
tc_conditions: Materialises when the same build runs in several environments, or a setting must change quickly in production. Assumes the config server is actually running and holds this service's configuration.

tc_benefit: Settings such as URLs, credentials and tuning values can change per environment or at run time from the config server without rebuilding or redeploying vets-service.
tc_conditions: Materialises when the same build runs in several environments (the profile-specific import suggests this) or when a setting must change quickly in production. Assumes the config server is deployed and serves vets-service properties.

tc_benefit: Visits-service settings such as URLs, credentials and tuning values can be changed per environment from the central config server without rebuilding or redeploying the service.
tc_conditions: Materialises when the same build runs in several environments, or when a setting must be changed quickly in production. Assumes the config server actually serves visits-service properties.
